convenience: The shop on our corner is a real convenience because it opens late.
We love the convenience of having a bus stop right outside our house.
For your convenience, the library has put a bench by the door.
existence: Nobody knew of the island's existence until someone found an old map.
Our teacher showed us a photo that proved the badger's existence.
Do you believe in the existence of life on other planets?
excellent: Well done, that was an excellent goal in the match!
She got full marks, which is an excellent result for a spelling test.
The weather was excellent, so we had a picnic on the beach.
frequently: We visit the library frequently, nearly every Saturday.
It rains frequently in autumn, so I always pack my coat.
My cat frequently sleeps on the warm windowsill after lunch.
sufficient: Is one blanket sufficient, or will you need another tonight?
Two scoops of flour were sufficient to make the small cake.
Do we have sufficient chairs for everyone at the party?
ancient: Is this crumbly old coin really from ancient times?
That ancient oak tree in the park is older than the town.
The ancient castle wall has stood on the hill for ages.
apparent: It is apparent from the droopy leaves that the plant needs water.
Her happiness was apparent from the big smile on her face.
The crack in the old mug was apparent as soon as I lifted it.
relevant: A picture of a robot is not relevant to our topic on butterflies.
Please keep your answer relevant to the question the teacher asked.
Which of these facts is relevant to our project about the seaside?
hindrance: Please move your bike so the post van can pass without hindrance.
With no hindrance at all, the kite rose high into the sky!
The ducks swam across the pond without any hindrance.
nuisance: What a nuisance, the sticky tape has run out again!
Is that squeaky gate a nuisance every time you open it?
The noisy leaf blower next door is such a nuisance on Sunday morning.
